service.description: What the database db allows the Tools screens, and why the rest is not available ("needs the pg_monitor role", "pg_stat_statements is not loaded"), probed once and kept five minutes; refresh probes again. features maps each of statementStats, activity, cancel, terminate, lockWaits, tableSizes, bloatExact, indexUsage, indexOnline, fkLightLock, maintenance, integrity, settings, settingsEdit and backups to available and reason (why not, or what limits it). backend is embedded-postgres, postgres, mysql or mariadb. available is false, with reason, when the database did not answer.

Forget the entity facade's statement stats of this instance (entity-facade@query-stats), as ec.entity.clearQueryStats() does. Needs the DATABASE_ADMIN permission, and writes a DbaStatsReset DatabaseAudit row.

Compare the entity model with the database (EntityDbMeta::compare): missing tables, missing, extra and differently typed columns, missing, extra and invalid indexes, missing and extra foreign keys, and on Postgres foreign keys no index leads with. entityNames empty compares every entity of the group. tables lists only the tables with a difference, each with entityName, groupName, tableName, missingTable, missingColumns, extraColumns, columnTypes, missingIndexes (with their ddl), extraIndexes, invalidIndexes, missingForeignKeys (with ddl), extraForeignKeys and unindexedForeignKeys.

The statements that bring a selection of the comparison's differences in line, in the online forms (§5.2): on Postgres CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS, ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, and an invalid index dropped and created again (REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY for one the model does not have); on MySQL ALGORITHM=INPLACE LOCK=NONE, and a unique index (a constraint there) is never dropped. changes is some of missingIndexes, invalidIndexes, extraIndexes (dropped), missingForeignKeys, extraForeignKeys (dropped) and dropForeignKeys (every key of the selected tables); empty is missingIndexes, invalidIndexes and missingForeignKeys. names limits the plan to these index and key names (one row). Each statement has statementSeqId (six digits), statementText, dependsOnSeqId, entityName, tableName, what and lockTimeout (whether it takes the job's lock timeout). With DATABASE_ADMIN the plan is stored as a Pending DatabaseJob (kind DbjDdl, a DbaJob audit row of its texts and creator) and jobId names it: run#DatabaseJob runs it as shown. Without, or with nothing to run, jobId is null and jobReason says why.

The two jobs that wrap a bulk load (Data › Load, Snapshots): dropJobId drops every foreign key of the selected entities' tables; restoreJobId makes them again after the load (Postgres from each key's own definition, NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; MySQL from the model). Both are stored as Pending jobs of kind DbjLoadWrap, as plan#SchemaChanges stores its plan.

The DDL of entityNames (every entity of the group when empty) in the database's dialect, from the builders the table check uses: CREATE TABLE (with the full-text columns), then the indexes, then the foreign keys among the selected entities; for Download DDL as fileName.

Run the plan job jobId, or run it again: queued on a service worker (out queued), or with wait here (out statusId and the counts). Its statements not Done run in order, each on a connection of its own outside a transaction that is closed after it, with no statement timeout, its backendPid and backendStart on its row. Every statement but the light forms (CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, REINDEX ... CONCURRENTLY, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT alone, VACUUM without FULL, ANALYZE) waits at most the job's lock timeout and is tried three more times; one whose dependsOnSeqId did not finish is DbjsSkipped; a failed one does not stop the others. An invalid index a failed CONCURRENTLY build left is dropped before the build runs again. The job moves to DbjsRunning only from the status read, so two runs cannot overlap; a job that is running, or was cancelled before it ran, is refused. At the end the job is DbjsDone, DbjsFailed (a statement failed or was skipped) or DbjsCancelled, its user is notified on topic DatabaseJob, a summary is logged and a DbaJob DatabaseAudit row names the runner. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN.

Cancel the job jobId. A Pending one (a plan not run, or one queued) is marked DbjsCancelled and does not run (how notStarted). A Running one is marked DbjsCancelled so no further statement starts, and its running statement is cancelled, with the canceller of this instance when it runs here (how local), else by its backendPid and backendStart with pg_cancel_backend, or KILL QUERY of the connection running the job's statement, on a connection of its own (how backend). One that ended, or changed since it was read, is cancelled false, how none. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaCancel DatabaseAudit row.

The job jobId (its DatabaseJob fields), its statements (DatabaseJobStatement fields), and for a statement running now the server's progress (Postgres pg_stat_progress_create_index, _vacuum, _analyze and _cluster; MySQL performance_schema.events_stages_current; MariaDB the PROCESSLIST progress) and the sessions blocking it (Postgres pg_blocking_pids joined to pg_stat_activity, MySQL sys.innodb_lock_waits, MariaDB INNODB_LOCK_WAITS). The jobs calls run a cleanup at most every five minutes: a Running job of an instance that is gone (this one, started before this process; another the cluster rows say is not live) is marked DbjsFailed ("the server stopped"), and a plan job never run for a day is deleted.
The latest database jobs, newest first, of statusId when given.

Each table's estimated rows, total, table and index bytes, live and dead rows, last vacuum, autovacuum, analyze and autoanalyze, sequential and index scans (Postgres), or the InnoDB estimates, free bytes and update time (MySQL), largest first, from one catalog query, each with entity_name. reason is the error when the query failed.
The exact row count of the table tableName (one the schema has).

The statements of a maintenance job on tableNames: action vacuumAnalyze (VACUUM (ANALYZE)), analyze, reindex (REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY), vacuumFull and cluster on Postgres, which take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and need allowExclusiveLock; analyze (ANALYZE TABLE) and optimize (OPTIMIZE TABLE) on MySQL and MariaDB. Out as plan#SchemaChanges: with DATABASE_ADMIN the plan is stored as a Pending job of kind DbjMaintenance named by jobId, which run#DatabaseJob runs.

The database's sessions (Postgres pg_stat_activity of this database; MySQL and MariaDB the PROCESSLIST) with state, wait event, query and transaction start and statement, each marked own_app (this instance's, by the application_name the drivers set to the instance id), idle_in_transaction_long (over a minute), running_long (over ten seconds), with blocked_by; and blockingChains, trees of pid and blocks from the sessions that wait on no one.

Cancel the statement of session pid (pg_cancel_backend, KILL QUERY). The pid must be a client session of this database (Postgres pg_stat_activity of current_database(), MySQL the PROCESSLIST), not a server worker; this app's own sessions (its application_name: the framework's, a database job's) need force. signalled is whether the server found the session. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaCancel DatabaseAudit row with force.
End session pid (pg_terminate_backend, KILL), with the checks and force of cancel#DatabaseSession. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaTerminate DatabaseAudit row with force.

The index checks of §4.2: unindexedForeignKeys (Postgres: keys no index leads with), unusedIndexes (not unique, never scanned since statsSince), duplicateIndexes (led by another index of the table, with covered_by), invalidIndexes (a failed CONCURRENTLY build), and the transaction id wraparound ages databaseAge and tableAge (Postgres).

The statements of sqlText as a run with Allow Changes needs them confirmed: each with changes (it may change data), ownTransaction (VACUUM, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, CREATE DATABASE: runs on its own), implicitCommit (MySQL DDL, which commits) and transactionControl; changeCount; and token, the one-time confirmation run#Sql or explain#Sql takes for this user, db and sqlText on any instance, good for ten minutes (moqui.database.SqlRunToken). On a production instance confirmDatabaseName is the name run#Sql needs typed. parameterNames are the :name parameters. Transaction control (COMMIT, ROLLBACK, BEGIN, SAVEPOINT, SET TRANSACTION, MySQL LOCK TABLES, SET autocommit, ...) is refused in every mode: a run is its own transaction.

Run sqlText, split into statements. Read only unless allowChanges, which needs the token of classify#Sql (spent by this run) and on production confirmDatabaseName. With changes the script is one transaction and stops at the first failure (rolledBack), unless eachOnOwn; a read-only script stops at its first failure too. parameters binds each :name as a value. limit rows per query (500, at most 100,000); offset fetches more of a single read-only query; timeoutSeconds (300, at most 3,600) cancels the statement running at the time. runId (8 to 36 letters, digits or -) names the run for cancel#SqlRun; one is made when empty, and one running on any instance is refused. A cancel or timeout with statements left rolls a transaction back. Every connection a run with changes used is closed after it, so no session state reaches later work. results has, per statement: seq, sql, givesRows, columns, records (lists of values), limitReached, rowsAffected, durationMs, error, rerunnable (a plain query run read only: may be run again to sort, filter or fetch more), skipped, rolledBack (it ran and was rolled back) and auditId. A refused attempt with changes (no or a spent token, the wrong name) is audited too.

Cancel the run runId: the user's own, or any with DATABASE_ADMIN. On this instance through its connection's canceller; a run on another instance is found by its running audit row and cancelled with pg_cancel_backend or KILL QUERY, once the session is checked to be the one the row recorded (Postgres backend_start, MySQL the server's start); a running row older than the longest timeout is ignored. outcome is cancelled, cancelledRemote (with instanceId and backendId) or notRunning. Refused under the read fence for a remote cancel. Writes a DbaCancel audit row.

The plan of one statement (§7.5): Postgres EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, BUFFERS), MySQL and MariaDB EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON. analyze runs it: Postgres adds ANALYZE, MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE (format text), MariaDB ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON. A statement that may change data then needs the token of classify#Sql (and on production confirmDatabaseName) and runs in a transaction that is rolled back (rolledBack), as every analyzed statement on MySQL and MariaDB does. Registered under runId for cancel#SqlRun, under timeoutSeconds as run#Sql. plan is the database's text (JSON when format is json).

The SQL editor's completion schema: tables (table name to its column names, a table outside the connection's schema as schema.table), entities (each entity of the group to its table) and dialect (postgres or mysql).

The database's own statement stats (§7.2), the most costly first, at most limit (100, at most 1,000). Postgres pg_stat_statements: query_id, query, calls, total_exec_time, mean_exec_time, rows, shared_blks_hit, shared_blks_read, temp_blks_written (milliseconds). MySQL and MariaDB events_statements_summary_by_digest: query_id, query, calls, sum_timer_wait (picoseconds), sum_rows_examined, sum_no_index_used. When they do not read, available is false with the reason of get#Capabilities.
Reset the database's own statement stats: pg_stat_statements_reset(), or a TRUNCATE of the digest table. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; refused under the read fence; writes a DbaStatsReset audit row.

The current user's own SQL audit rows, newest first (limit 50, at most 500), of db when given: the SQL screen's history. Each has auditId, db, statementText, isChange, rowsReturned, rowsAffected, durationMs, errorText and startTime.
The user's own saved queries and the shared ones (of db when given), by description: queryId, description, db, sqlText, ownerUserId, isShared, parametersJson.
Create a saved query (no queryId), owned by the current user, or update one the user owns. parametersJson, when given, is JSON (the :name parameters' defaults).
Delete a saved query the current user owns.

Delete the DatabaseAudit rows older than the database_audit_days property (90 by default, at least 1), and the expired SqlRunToken rows: the DatabaseAuditPurge ServiceJob, which runs with no user signed in; a signed-in caller needs DATABASE_ADMIN.

The grid's columns, each: name, title, type (text, long-text, number, date, time, date-time, indicator, boolean, binary), editable, editor (input, textarea, number, date, time, datetime, tickCross, list; null when not editable), pk, encrypted (shown masked, never edited), notNull, createOnly, maxLength, relatedEntity and relatedField (the lookup's), and field (an editable SQL result's entity field). entityName is the entity the grid saves to: the source's, or a SQL result's whose columns are all of one table with its entity's whole primary key and its lastUpdatedStamp, in the group's schema, from a statement that names the table once with no JOIN, set operation, DISTINCT, GROUP BY or subquery (§9.5); null when read only, with readOnlyReason. hasStamp: each row has _stamp, which save sends back. keyColumns and stampColumn: an editable SQL result's key and stamp columns, for the source spec. A SQL column's type is that of its first value that is not null.

One page for Tabulator's progressive load: page from 1, size (100, at most 1,000). last_page is page plus one while pages come back full, and the page itself once one is short, with last_row the row count then; no count is run. For an unfiltered entity source last_row is the catalog's estimate while more pages come (estimated true). Each row of data is a map of the columns; an entity row has its primary key and _stamp (its lastUpdatedStamp) too; encrypted fields are masked.
Count rows: an entity find count, or count(*) over the wrapped SQL, with the source's conditions and filter.

The whole source (conditions, filter, sort, columns) as format csv (default) or xlsx, written to location: under the user's own runtime://tmp/grid-export/(userId)/ or dbresource://moqui/database/export/(userId)/, with DATABASE_ADMIN also any dbresource:// location or one under runtime://export/, never component://, file: or other runtime:// places; when empty a new location under runtime://tmp/grid-export/(userId)/, which the screen sends as a download after checking that the userId of its path is the current user's (the cleanup job removes those files after a day). An entity source is read through the find's cursor and CSV written row by row; XLSX is built in memory and stops at 100,000 rows; a SQL source stops at 200,000 rows; truncated says so. Encrypted fields are masked.

The options of a related-entity column (field of entityName, whose one relationship has it as the single key): the related rows whose key or label holds term, ignoring case, 20 at a time from offset. Each option has value and label (the related entity's description, else a ...Name field, with the key).

Save the grid's changes to entityName in one transaction: updates [{pk, stamp, fields}] (only the edited fields), creates [{fields}], deletes [{pk, stamp}], each through the entity's update#, create# or delete# (its authorization, validation, ECA rules and audit log apply). stamp is the row's _stamp, required for an update or delete of an entity with lastUpdatedStamp; a row changed since, gone, or not visible to the user is refused alike (conflict, "The row was changed or removed by someone else since you loaded it: reload it"). createdKeys: the primary key of each created row, in the order of creates. Every row is checked before any is written; a refused row rolls back every other. saved is true only when everything was saved; refused lists each refused row: kind (update, create, delete), index (in its list), pk, message, fieldErrors (field to message) and conflict. Views, the identity and secret entities, UserAccount's secret fields, encrypted fields, key fields of an update and lastUpdatedStamp are refused. Writes a DbaGridSave audit row with the entity and the counts, not the values.
The user's own grid views and the shared ones, by description: viewId, description, ownerUserId, isShared, sourceJson, layoutJson.
Create a grid view (no viewId), owned by the current user, or update one the user owns. sourceJson (required) and layoutJson (columns, widths, order, frozen, filters, sort) are JSON.
Delete a grid view the current user owns.
